# Every "take the first of the tied ones" is a way for input order to decide
# the output. ECFP ignores stereochemistry, so stereoisomers score identically,
# and deduplication silently became selection by file position until this was
# added. The shuffle control went from 80% back to 100%.
def rank_key(i, scores, props):
    """Sort key: score first, then a property of the molecule itself.

    Scores alone are not enough to order the list. ECFP does not encode
    stereochemistry, so stereoisomers receive identical scores, and any
    "take the first" step over them -- choosing a representative, cutting the
    top N -- would be settled by the order the rows happened to arrive in.
    That order is not neutral here: the library's leading rows carry 2.27x the
    base hit rate. Breaking ties on the InChIKey removes the question.
    """
    return (-scores[i], props[i]["inchikey"] or "", i)

# Stops rather than continues when most of the input will not parse. This
    # fired on GramNegAccum at 45.5% and the cause was a notation dialect, not
    # broken chemistry; without it the dataset would have silently shrunk.
    failures = dropped["smiles_unparseable"] + dropped["smiles_missing"]
    total = rows + sum(v for k, v in dropped.items() if k != "out_of_scope")
    if total and failures / total > MAX_PARSE_FAILURE_RATE:
        sys.exit(
            f"{src}: {failures}/{total} SMILES unparseable ({failures/total:.2%}), "
            f"above the {MAX_PARSE_FAILURE_RATE:.0%} limit. The descriptor pipeline is "
            f"more likely at fault than the data; stopping instead of continuing."
        )

# This caught a real failure: 78% of a library shared one score because the
# logistic function had saturated in f32, the sort fell back on file order,
# and the file order was itself enriched for hits. The result looked like a
# permeability effect and was reported as one.
def assert_ranking_is_usable(scores, tag, max_tie=MAX_TIE_SHARE,
                             min_distinct=MIN_DISTINCT_SHARE):
    """Refuses a score array that cannot order its rows; returns the diagnostics."""
    counts = Counter(scores)
    value, n = counts.most_common(1)[0]
    tie_share = n / len(scores)
    distinct_share = len(counts) / len(scores)
    if tie_share > max_tie:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{tag}: {n}/{len(scores)} rows ({tie_share:.1%}) share the score "
            f"{value!r}, above the {max_tie:.0%} limit. Ranking them would order "
            f"by file position, not by the model. Rank on the logit, and check "
            f"how far this data sits from what the model was fitted to."
        )
    if distinct_share < min_distinct:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{tag}: only {len(counts)}/{len(scores)} distinct scores "
            f"({distinct_share:.1%}), below the {min_distinct:.0%} limit. Most "
            f"comparisons would be decided by file position rather than by score."
        )
    return {"tie_share": tie_share, "distinct_share": distinct_share}

#
# Structure, because behaviour could not be locked here and saying so is the
# point.
#
# This was marked `pbt` first, to fix what the function RETURNS over ten
# thousand inputs rather than how it is written -- the right shape for a rule
# whose three unit-tested cases can all be satisfied by an implementation that
# still has the asymmetry wrong. The vendored engine reported a pass on an
# implementation reduced to `return "answerable"`.
#
# It generates one integer argument, execs the region in an empty namespace,
# and swallows every exception from the call. rank_verdict takes three
# arguments and reads two module constants, so all ten thousand calls raised
# TypeError, were skipped, and the run ended green. A check that cannot fail
# is worse than no check: it is the shape that let `unittest discover` report
# success having run nothing, twice this week.
#
# So the lock is structural, which does stop a silent rewrite, and the
# behaviour is held by a property test over generated inputs in
# tests/test_contraindications.py, where the generation can be written for
# this function's actual signature.
def rank_verdict(distinct_share, top_share, sampled):
    """A SAMPLE CAN REFUSE A SET AND CANNOT CLEAR ONE.

    The distinct share rises as fewer molecules are measured: collisions get
    rarer when there are fewer pairs to collide. Measured on two independent
    sets, every step down in count raised it --

        430 survivors:    n=100 0.780  n=200 0.675  n=400 0.4975  n=430 0.486
      1,820 survivors:  n=1200 0.5967  n=1500 0.5253  n=1820 0.4648

    -- so a sampled figure behaves as an UPPER BOUND on the figure the whole
    set would give. That makes the two directions unequal:

      below the floor on a sample -> the full set is also below -> the refusal
        can be stated from the sample. This is what the module was built on:
        deciding that a model CANNOT order a set does not need every row.

      above the floor on a sample -> the full set may be below it, and here
        was: 1,200 of 1,820 gave 0.5967 and passed, and all 1,820 gave 0.4648
        and did not. The pass was the sample, not the model.

    The old code took the docstring's licence for the first case and applied
    it to the second. Of six runs, the one specification whose survivor set
    was larger than the sample was the only one reported rankable.

    Both directions lean on the bound holding, which is OBSERVED IN TWO SETS
    AND NOT PROVEN, so a sampled verdict says so either way. The risks are not
    symmetric -- claiming an order exists is worse than denying one that does
    -- but neither branch is assumption-free, and declining to call the
    monotonicity a theorem means disclosing where it is being relied on.

    Separated from rankability() so the rule can be tested without a model, a
    library and twelve minutes of fingerprinting. It is the whole of the
    decision; rankability() measures the two shares and hands them here.
    """
    clears = distinct_share >= MIN_DISTINCT_SHARE and top_share <= MAX_TIE_SHARE
    if not clears:
        return "not_answerable"
    return "not_settled_at_this_sample" if sampled else "answerable"

# UNLOCK_REASON (2026-10-08): AssignStereochemistry added alongside
        # RemoveHs. Both lines restore a step that Chem.MolFromSmiles performs
        # for itself and the sanitize=False path above skips. Neither is
        # optional and neither belongs to the repair.
        #
        # RemoveHs: without it the graph keeps [H] atoms and every descriptor
        # shifts on any input that writes one. This looked like the valence
        # repair changing CHAMP, and CHAMP has no atom the repair touches.
        #
        # AssignStereochemistry: without it ring double-bond stereo is never
        # perceived. MolToSmiles writes the bond directions back either way, so
        # the canonical SMILES is identical and a SMILES-level comparison sees
        # nothing -- but InChI reads the flags, and py/candidates.py breaks ties
        # on the InChIKey. One IMI molecule with a ring `/C=C\` picked a
        # different stereoisomer as its representative because of this.
        mol = Chem.RemoveHs(mol)
        Chem.AssignStereochemistry(mol, cleanIt=True, force=True)
